content.title: About
content.content: Doughnuts are small fried or baked pastries made from yeast‑leavened dough (type 2834). The dough typically contains wheat flour, sugar, milk, eggs, and butter. After rising, the dough is shaped into rings or balls and fried in oil until golden, then coated with glaze, powdered sugar, or sprinkles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Doughnuts originated in Europe in the 19th century and quickly became popular in the United States, where they are called "donuts".
Traditional preparation involves deep‑frying, but baking has become popular in recent years as a lower‑calorie alternative.
There are countless fillings: jam, custard, chocolate, caramel, and even savory options with cheese.
In Japan, colorful "pop‑mats" doughnuts covered with bright glazes and toppings are a trend.
In the U.S., the first Monday of June is celebrated as National Donut Day.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Doughnuts provide rapid energy from carbohydrates, which can be useful for short‑term fuel needs.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Yeast in the dough supplies modest amounts of B1, B2, and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and iron
items.content: Milk and eggs add calcium and iron, essential for bone health and blood formation.

items.title: High sugar and fat
items.content: Traditional doughnuts are rich in sugar and saturated fat, which can contribute to weight gain and elevated cholesterol.

items.title: Gluten and dairy allergies
items.content: Because the recipe uses wheat flour and milk, people with these allergies should avoid them.

items.title: Trans fats from frying
items.content: Repeated use of frying oil can create trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Doughnuts are usually served warm and eaten as a snack or dessert, often paired with coffee or milk. They are commonly glazed, topped with sprinkles, nuts, or filled with cream or jam.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store doughnuts in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months; reheat in an oven or microwave before eating.
